A1.justification: Both complete, readable 21-page PDFs describe the same DiT-ST work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and references support reliable comparison. Neither contains a separately labeled appendix; the additional visualizations on pages 12–17 were included.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenEval and COCO experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and generated-image comparisons in Section 4, Tables 1–10, and Figures 6–10.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and generated-image comparisons, including the visualizations following the conclusion.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same caption parsing, hierarchical input construction, text-encoding refinement, incremental primitive injection, timestep selection, and training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use SAM-LLaVA for training and GenEval, COCO-5K, and COCO-30K for evaluation. Caption-length coverage and the qualitative generation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each benchmark, caption-form experiment, and visual comparison. This includes DALL-E 3 and Dream Engine in Table 2 and HunyuanDiT in Figure 9.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the 100K training subset, 2B/8B model variants, evaluation samples, GenEval/FID/CLIPScore metrics, and 40-step inference procedure. Ablation settings also match.

E4.justification: The caption-length analysis in Table 5 and ablations of hierarchical input, injection presence, primitive order, injection timesteps, and sliding-window size in Tables 6–10 are unchanged. The qualitative examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, experimental seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–10 and all qualitative results match. For example, DiT-ST Medium retains GenEval 0.69 and COCO-5K CLIPScore 34.09/FID 22.11; DiT-ST Large retains COCO-30K FID 17.16.

T1.justification: The caption-graph definitions, token construction, attention-convergence calculations, SNR-curvature reasoning, and loss equations (1–10) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about mitigating complete-text comprehension defects through split-text conditioning, improving semantic fidelity, and providing parameter-efficient, architecture-agnostic benefits.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of results are unchanged. Section 3.3.1 retains the qualifications concerning gradual, sample-dependent semantic emergence and the computational cost of selecting timesteps separately for each sample.

D1.justification: The parser and encoder choices, thresholds, injection windows, inference details, and statement about released training CSV files remain unchanged. No additional implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 and references [1–55] retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the discussion of LongAlign and SCoPE. The conference-footer update does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 changes Changwei Wang’s affiliation from Tongji University to Shandong Academy of Sciences, removes the equal-contribution note, changes the corresponding-author marker, and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Front-page changes produce modest reflow across pages 1–4, including shifted abstract boundaries and vertical placement of existing figures. All ten figures and ten tables retain their content, captions, and display structures.

improvement.justification: The affiliation, contribution-note, and conference-footer updates accompany only minor layout changes. The method, experimental evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, with no material improvement or deterioration in readability or scientific support.
